title: Best Herb Scissors for Heavy Duty Restaurant Prep
meta_description: Discover the top professional herb shears for heavy‑duty restaurant prep. Learn why five‑blade Herb Scissors are the go‑to tool for chefs who need speed, precis
html:
When you’re running a line that dishes out fresh salsa, garnish‑heavy pasta, or herb‑infused sauces, the speed and consistency of your prep can make or break service. That's why professional herb shears are a staple in any high‑volume kitchen. A good pair of scissors lets you mince cilantro, chives, basil, and other delicate greens in seconds, without bruising the leaves or creating a mess on the cutting board. Below, we break down the features you need in a heavy‑duty pair of herb scissors and why the five‑blade Herb Scissors stand out for restaurant‑scale prep.

What Sets Professional Herb Shears Apart?

Not all scissors are created equal. The best professional herb shears combine a few key design elements that keep them functional, durable, and easy to clean:

  • Blade configuration: Multiple thin blades cut the herb into uniform pieces in a single motion, eliminating the need for a separate chopping board.
  • Ergonomic handles: Heavy‑duty kitchens demand tools that feel comfortable after dozens of repetitions. Textured grips and a balanced pivot reduce hand fatigue.
  • Stainless‑steel construction: Corrosion‑resistant blades survive frequent exposure to acid‑rich herbs and the occasional splash of hot oil.
  • Easy‑clean design: A built‑in cleaning comb or removable blade guard prevents stray bits from sticking, speeding up turnaround between stations.

When these features come together, you get a tool that can handle a full‑service rush without slowing you down.

Why the Five‑Blade Herb Scissors Are Ideal for Restaurant Prep

The Herb Scissors feature a unique five‑blade arrangement that slices cilantro, chives, basil, and similar greens into fine, even pieces with just one snip. The blades are spaced to create a consistent bite‑size that’s perfect for garnishes and sauces. Because the cutting action is so efficient, chefs can keep the ingredient in the pan or bowl, minimizing transfer steps and preserving flavor.

Another standout feature is the integrated cleaning comb. After you’ve minced a bunch of basil, simply run the comb through the blades to dislodge any stubborn fibers. This design eliminates the need to soak the scissors or scrub them with a brush, which is a huge time‑saver during a busy service.

Stainless‑steel blades are forged to a high hardness rating, so they stay sharp even after repeated use. The handles are contoured with a non‑slip rubber overlay, providing a secure grip when hands are wet or oily. Together, these details make the Herb Scissors a reliable workhorse for any professional kitchen.

How to Use Herb Scissors Effectively

Even the best scissors can feel awkward if you don’t use them correctly. Follow these steps to get the most out of your professional herb shears:

  1. Gather the herb: Rinse and pat dry the leaves. For larger herbs like basil, stack the leaves in a loose pile; for tiny herbs like chives, a small bunch works best.
  2. Position the blades: Hold the scissors with the blades open and align the herb just above the hinge. The five blades will automatically create a uniform cut as they close.
  3. Snip in a fluid motion: Use a smooth, steady motion rather than a jerky one. This ensures each leaf is cut cleanly without tearing.
  4. Collect the mince: The herbs will fall directly into your bowl, pan, or sauce pot. No need to transfer from a cutting board.
  5. Clean immediately: Run the included cleaning comb through the blades while the herbs are still fresh. This prevents the green juices from hardening and keeps the scissors ready for the next batch.

Practicing this routine a few times will make the process feel as natural as chopping with a knife, but with far less waste and cleanup.

Maintenance Tips for Longevity

Professional herb shears see a lot of action, so proper care extends their lifespan:

  • Rinse the blades under warm water immediately after use to remove any residue.
  • Use the cleaning comb to dislodge tiny fragments that might stick between the blades.
  • Dry the scissors thoroughly before storing them to avoid moisture buildup.
  • Periodically sharpen the blades with a fine‑grade sharpening stone if you notice a loss of cutting efficiency.

Following these simple steps keeps the Herb Scissors performing at peak efficiency, even during back‑to‑back service nights.

Alternative Options and When to Upgrade

If your kitchen currently uses a basic pair of kitchen shears, you’ll notice a clear difference when you switch to professional herb shears. The multi‑blade design not only speeds up prep but also produces a more consistent texture, which can affect the final dish’s presentation and mouthfeel. However, if you only need occasional herb prep for a small café, a single‑blade herb cutter might suffice. For any operation that handles bulk herb preparation—think Mexican, Mediterranean, or farm‑to‑table restaurants—the Herb Scissors are the upgrade that pays for itself in labor savings.

FAQ

Can I use the Herb Scissors on tougher greens like kale or spinach?

The five‑blade design is optimized for delicate herbs. While you can run softer greens like spinach through them, tougher leaves such as kale may jam the blades and dull them faster. For sturdy greens, stick to a chef’s knife or a dedicated vegetable slicer.

Are the blades dishwasher safe?

Yes, the stainless‑steel blades can be placed in the top rack of a dishwasher, but hand‑washing and using the built‑in cleaning comb is recommended for the quickest turnaround during service.

How often should I sharpen the blades?

In a high‑volume kitchen, you’ll likely need to touch‑up the edge after a few weeks of daily use. A fine‑grade sharpening stone or a professional sharpening service will keep the herb shears cutting cleanly without replacing them.
